info.title: Binge Server API
info.description:
HTTP API of the Binge comic server.

Every route except `/health`, `/setup` and `/sign-in` takes a session cookie or an API token, and answers 401 with the code `unauthorized` without a good one. Routes that manage accounts (`/me/password`, `/tokens`, `/users`) take a session only.

get.summary: Returns one book.

put.summary:
Makes a page of a book the cover of a book, in place of its first page.
Only the owner can.
put.description:
The cover goes with the book's identity: every copy of the book shows
it, and it is still the book's when its file is moved or renamed. The
book's `cover` names the new image.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The book the cover is for

400.description: The page is no picture the server can read, or the book's file could not be read

403.description: The caller is not the owner

404.description: No such book, or no such page

delete.summary:
Takes back the cover chosen for a book, which shows its first page
again. Nothing happens when none was chosen. Only the owner can.

204.description: The book shows its first page

403.description: The caller is not the owner

put.summary:
Makes a picture the cover of a book: the request's body is a JPEG, PNG,
WebP or GIF file of 20 MB at most. Only the owner can.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The book the cover is for

400.description: Not a picture the server can read, one of more than 20 MB, or the book's file could not be read

403.description: The caller is not the owner

get.summary:
Returns who a book names as its writers and pencillers, as people: the
names in the book's `info` are only what its file spells.

Lists the pages of a book that are favorites of the caller's, by their
numbers from 0, in reading order.

Says what comes after a book where the caller reads it, for a reader to
go on to at the book's last page.
get.description:
Reading follows where the book was opened from: the reading list named
by `list`; with `group`, the book's group of its series, which ends
with the group; and otherwise its series, on from one group to the
next.

parameters.name: list
parameters.description: The reading list the book was opened from.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description:
Whether the book was opened from its group of its series. Counts
for nothing when `list` is given, or when the book is in no group.

404.description: No such book, or no such reading list

get.summary:
Lists the pages of a book in reading order, with the sizes a reader needs
to lay them out. The images are at `/pages/{identity}/{number}`.

put.summary:
Puts a book where the body says, and answers with the book as it is then.
The series and the group must be there already: this makes neither. Only
the owner can.

400.description: There is no such series or group, the group is in another series, the series is in another library, the date is not written as asked, or the file could not be read

403.description: The caller is not the owner

put.summary:
Records how far the caller has read a book. Reaching the last page completes
the book; reading it again from an earlier page takes that back.
put.description:
A reader saves each page as it is shown. The saves are also the record
of when the caller read: pages of one book saved less than half an hour
apart count as one sitting.

400.description: The page is not in the book

get.summary:
Lists the reading lists the caller sees that a book is in, in name
order.

put.summary:
Sets a file that could not be read aside: seen, and no longer listed
with the others or counted. The file is not touched. A scan that reads
it again and still cannot lists it again. Only the owner can.

400.description: The book can be read

403.description: The caller is not the owner

delete.summary: Takes a file back from the ones set aside. Only the owner can.

400.description: The book can be read

403.description: The caller is not the owner

get.summary:
Lists the collections the caller sees, in name order: their own, and the
ones shared with them or with everyone. A collection of someone else's
that holds no series the caller may read is left out.

parameters.name: on_home
parameters.description: Only the ones that are rows on Home.

post.summary:
Makes a collection of the caller's own, with the series named in it from
the start. Nobody else sees it until it is shared.
post.description:
Every series named must be on the server: one that is not refuses the
request, and nothing is made. A series named twice is in the collection
once. One request names 10,000 at most.

400.description: The name or the summary cannot be used, or a series named is not on the server

409.description: Another collection of the caller's has the name; `conflicts_with` is its id

get.summary: Returns one collection.

delete.summary:
Deletes a collection. Its series are not touched. Only the one whose
collection it is can.

403.description: The collection is someone else's

patch.summary:
Gives a collection another name and summary. Its series stay. Only the
one whose collection it is can.

400.description: The name or the summary cannot be used

403.description: The collection is someone else's

409.description: Another collection of the caller's has the name; `conflicts_with` is its id

put.summary:
Makes a collection a row on Home, or no longer one. Only the one whose
collection it is can. It is a row for everyone who sees the collection,
with the series they may read: a collection shared with everyone is a
row on everyone's Home. Each person puts the row where they want it, or
away.

403.description: The collection is someone else's

get.summary: Lists the series of a collection the caller may read, in name order.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many, from the first by name. All of them when left out.

post.summary:
Puts the series named in a collection. A series it already holds stays.
Only the one whose collection it is can.
post.description:
Every series named must be on the server: one that is not refuses the
request, and nothing is added. One request names 10,000 at most.

400.description: A series named is not on the server

403.description: The collection is someone else's

delete.summary:
Takes a series out of a collection. Only the one whose collection it is
can.

403.description: The collection is someone else's

404.description: No such collection, or the series is not in it

put.summary:
Says who a collection is shared with from now on: everyone, the people
named, or nobody. Only the one whose collection it is can. The people it
is shared with see it, with the series they may read, and cannot change
it. Someone who may read none of its series does not see it.
put.description:
Everyone named must be on the server: someone who is not refuses the
request, and nothing changes. Naming the one whose collection it is
changes nothing.

400.description: Someone named is not on the server

403.description: The collection is someone else's

get.summary:
Lists the books the caller started and did not finish, the one read last
first.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
How many entries to return at most. 24 when left out, never more
than 100.

get.summary:
Returns a cover image. A cover never changes under its name, so it can be
cached for good.

parameters.name: cover
parameters.description: The `cover` of a series or book

delete.summary:
Deletes a group that holds no books. One that holds books is refused:
move them first. Only the owner can.

403.description: The caller is not the owner

patch.summary:
Gives a group another number or name. Its kind and its books stay. Only
the owner can.

400.description: The number or name is not one a group may have

403.description: The caller is not the owner

409.description: The series has a group of that kind, number and name; `conflicts_with` is its id

get.summary:
Lists the books of a group in the order they are read: by issue number,
and the books without one by the date they were published.

Returns one group of a series seen whole, for the page that presents it:
the group, its series, what its books say about it together, how far the
caller is through it, and the book to open next.

Reports the server's version and build, whether its database responds, and whether
first-run setup is still to do. Open to anyone: it is how a client finds
out that this is a Binge server before it has signed in.
Lists the libraries the caller may read, in name order.

post.summary: Adds a folder as a library and starts scanning it. Only the owner can.

400.description: The path is not a folder the server can read

403.description: The caller is not the owner

409.description: The folder is already a library

get.summary: Returns one library with the state of its scan.

delete.summary:
Removes a library from the server. The folder and its files are not
touched. Only the owner can.

403.description: The caller is not the owner

get.summary: Lists what the series of a library can be narrowed by.

Lists the books a library holds more than once, each with its files, in
name order. Two files are one book when their pages are the same,
whatever their names and tags, so a copy that was retagged is found too.
The server deletes no file: which copy to keep is for the owner to do in
the folder. Only the owner can ask.

403.description: The caller is not the owner

put.summary:
Says what a library makes from what its files say from now on. Only the
owner can.
put.description:
What is turned on is made at once, from what the last scan found the
files to say. What is turned off makes nothing more: the reading lists
and collections there are stay.

403.description: The caller is not the owner

post.summary:
Starts scanning a library for added, changed and removed files. Does
nothing when a scan of it is already running. Only the owner can.

403.description: The caller is not the owner

get.summary:
Lists the scans that changed what a library holds, the latest first.
A scan that found the library as it was is not listed, and only the
latest fifty are kept. Only the owner can ask.

403.description: The caller is not the owner

get.summary:
Lists a part of the series of a library: those the narrowing leaves in,
in the order asked for, with how many there are in all.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
What to order the series by. By name when left out. Series the order
says nothing about, such as one with no year, come last.

schema.description: What a library's series are ordered by.

parameters.name: seed
parameters.description:
Which of the orders `sort=random` gives. Keep it while reading the
list a part at a time.

parameters.name: read
parameters.description: How far the caller is through the series.

items.description: How far the caller is through a series.
How far the caller is through a series.

parameters.name: publisher
parameters.description: A publisher, as the books name it.

parameters.name: year
parameters.description: A year a book came out, as `1993`, or the ten from one, as `1990s`.

parameters.name: writer
parameters.description: The id of a person a book names as a writer.

parameters.name: penciller
parameters.description: The id of a person a book names as a penciller.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: How many to pass over, from the start of the list.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many to answer with: 100 when left out, 500 at most.

400.description: A year is not written as one

post.summary: Adds a series with no books to a library. Only the owner can.

400.description: The name cannot be used

403.description: The caller is not the owner

409.description: Another series of the library has the name; `conflicts_with` is its id

get.summary:
Lists the letters the names of a library's series start with, for
jumping through the list by name: only the letters some series has, in
the order of the list. Takes the narrowing `GET /libraries/{id}/series`
takes and counts the series it leaves in; of the rest it reads `reverse`
only.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description:
What to order the series by. By name when left out. Series the order
says nothing about, such as one with no year, come last.

schema.description: What a library's series are ordered by.

parameters.name: seed
parameters.description:
Which of the orders `sort=random` gives. Keep it while reading the
list a part at a time.

parameters.name: read
parameters.description: How far the caller is through the series.

items.description: How far the caller is through a series.
How far the caller is through a series.

parameters.name: publisher
parameters.description: A publisher, as the books name it.

parameters.name: year
parameters.description: A year a book came out, as `1993`, or the ten from one, as `1990s`.

parameters.name: writer
parameters.description: The id of a person a book names as a writer.

parameters.name: penciller
parameters.description: The id of a person a book names as a penciller.

400.description: A year is not written as one

get.summary:
Lists the files of a library that could not be read, each with the reason
in `problem`, in the order of their paths. They are in no series. The
ones the owner set aside are left out, or are the ones listed when
`set_aside` is given, which only the owner can ask for.

parameters.name: set_aside
parameters.description:
Lists the ones the owner set aside, in place of the ones still to
look at.

403.description: The caller is not the owner and asks for the ones set aside

get.summary:
Returns who makes the request. This is also how an app finds out whether
its token still works.

Lists a part of the caller's favorite pages, with how many there are in
all: series by series in the order of their names, and inside a series
book by book as they are read. The pages of books in no series come
last. A page of a book that is not on the server now is left out, and is
listed again when its book is back.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: How many to pass over, from the start of the list.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many to answer with: 100 when left out, 500 at most.

put.summary:
Changes the caller's own password. Their sessions in other browsers end;
this one and their tokens stay.

400.description: The current password is wrong, or the new one will not do

403.description: The request came with a token

get.summary:
Tells what the caller read in a year: the days they read, the books
and pages of each month, and the writers they read most.

parameters.name: year
parameters.description: The year to look back on, on the caller's clock.

parameters.name: minutes_ahead
parameters.description:
How far the caller's clock is ahead of UTC, in minutes: `-180` three
hours behind. It says where their days start. UTC when left out.

400.description: The year or the clock is not one

get.summary: Lists everything the caller chose.

put.summary: Keeps a value under a key for the caller, in place of the one before.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: 1 to 64 lower-case letters, digits, dots, dashes or underscores

400.description: The key is not written as one, the value is too long, or the caller keeps too many

delete.summary: Forgets what the caller kept under a key. Nothing kept there is no error.

get.summary: Returns a page image exactly as the book's file stores it.
get.description:
The address is made of the book's `identity` and the page's `number`, so
the image under it never changes: it can be cached for good, and stays
valid when the book's file is moved or renamed.

304.description: The copy named by `If-None-Match` is still good

404.description: No such page, or the book's file is gone

409.description: The book's file changed since it was scanned

put.summary:
Makes a page a favorite of the caller's. A page that already is one
stays as it was.

400.description: The caller has 5,000 favorite pages already

delete.summary:
Makes a page no longer a favorite of the caller's. A page that was not
one is no error.

204.description: The page is not a favorite

get.summary:
Returns a page as a small picture: a JPEG that fits 320 by 480 pixels,
for a strip of pages to jump by or a card that shows one page.
get.description:
Like the page itself, it never changes under its address and can be
cached for good. The server makes it each time it is asked and keeps no
copy.

304.description: The copy named by `If-None-Match` is still good

400.description: The page is no picture the server can make smaller

404.description: No such page, or the book's file is gone

409.description: The book's file changed since it was scanned

get.summary:
Lists a part of the people the books the caller may read name, the ones
most books name first, with how many there are in all. With `q`, only
those one of whose names holds every word of it: the way to find the
two spellings of one person before making them one.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description:
Words to find people by: every one of them in one of their names.
Case and accents do not matter. Left out or empty, everyone.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: How many to pass over, from the start of the list.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many to answer with: 100 when left out, 500 at most.

get.summary: Returns one person with the names they go by.

patch.summary: Shows a person by another of their names. Only the owner can.

403.description: The caller is not the owner

404.description: No such person, or the name is not theirs

get.summary:
Lists a part of the books that name the person, from the first that
came out, with how many there are in all. The ones that say no date come
last, by series and number.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: How many to pass over, from the start of the list.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many to answer with: 100 when left out, 500 at most.

post.summary:
Makes several people one. The people named are gone and their names
become names of this one, who keeps the name they are shown by. No file
is touched, and `DELETE /people/{id}/names/{name}` takes a name back
out. Only the owner can.

400.description: Nobody is named, or the person themself

403.description: The caller is not the owner

404.description: One of the people is not there

post.summary:
Gives a person one more name, for the files that will spell them so. A
name that is already theirs changes nothing. Only the owner can.

400.description: The name is blank or too long

403.description: The caller is not the owner

409.description: Someone else goes by the name: `conflicts_with` is who

delete.summary:
Makes one of a person's names a person of its own again, and answers
with that person. The books that spell the name so follow it. The name
a person is shown by cannot leave them. Only the owner can.

400.description: It is the name they are shown by

403.description: The caller is not the owner

404.description: No such person, or the name is not theirs

get.summary: Lists the series that hold a book that names the person, in name order.

post.summary:
Marks books as read by the caller, or as unread: the books named, and
every book of the groups, series and reading lists named.
post.description:
A book marked read is as if the caller had reached its last page now; one
they had read already keeps the time they read it. A book marked unread
is as if they had never opened it. What is not on the server, what the
caller may not read, and files that could not be read are passed over, so
the answer says how many books changed. One request names 10,000 books,
groups, series and lists at most.

400.description: More than 10,000 were named

get.summary:
Lists the reading lists the caller sees, in name order: their own, and
the ones shared with them or with everyone. A list of someone else's
that holds no book the caller may read is left out.

post.summary:
Makes a reading list of the caller's own, with the books named in it
from the start. Nobody else sees it until it is shared.
post.description:
Every book, group, series and list named must be on the server: one that
is not, or a file that could not be read, refuses the request, and
nothing is made. A book named twice is in the list once. One request
names 10,000 at most.

400.description: The name or the summary cannot be used, or something named is not on the server

409.description: Another list of the caller's has the name; `conflicts_with` is its id

post.summary:
Reads a CBL file, the reading list format of ComicRack, and says which
book of the server each of its entries means and how that was found. It
makes nothing: the list is made with `POST /reading-lists`, from the
books settled on. The books are looked for among those the caller may
read.
post.description:
The request's body is the file, of 5 MB and 5,000 entries at most. An
entry's series is looked for by its name, by its name with the volume,
without its article, and without the words for a kind of publication,
in that order, until one finds a book with the entry's number. Among
several books with the number, the entry's volume and year decide. A
rule the caller kept with `POST /reading-lists/import/rules` comes
before all of this.

400.description: Not a CBL file the server can read, one that lists no books, or one too big

post.summary:
Keeps what the caller says an entry of a CBL file means, for their
imports from now on: which series its series is, or which book the
entry is. It takes the place of the rule they kept before for the same.
Each person has their own rules.

400.description: Neither or both of a series and a book were given, or the one given is not on the server

delete.summary: Forgets a rule the caller kept for their imports.

get.summary:
Returns one reading list seen whole, for the page that presents it: the
list, what its books say together, how far the caller is through it, and
the book to open next.

delete.summary:
Deletes a reading list. Its books are not touched, nor is anyone's
progress in them. Only the one whose list it is can.

403.description: The list is someone else's

patch.summary:
Gives a reading list another name and summary. Its books stay. Only the
one whose list it is can.

400.description: The name or the summary cannot be used

403.description: The list is someone else's

409.description: Another list of the caller's has the name; `conflicts_with` is its id

get.summary:
Lists the books of a reading list in the list's order: the ones that are
on the server now and the caller may read. A book whose pages the server
holds in two files is listed once.

post.summary:
Puts the books named at the end of a reading list, in the order they are
named. A book the list already holds stays where it is. Only the one
whose list it is can.
post.description:
Every book, group, series and list named must be on the server: one that
is not, or a file that could not be read, refuses the request, and
nothing is added. One request names 10,000 at most.

400.description: Something named is not on the server, or is a file that could not be read

403.description: The list is someone else's

delete.summary:
Takes a book out of a reading list. The others keep their order. Only
the one whose list it is can.

403.description: The list is someone else's

404.description: No such list or book, or the book is not in the list

put.summary:
Moves a book of a reading list to another position in it. The other
books keep their order. Only the one whose list it is can.

400.description: The position is below 0

403.description: The list is someone else's

404.description: No such list or book, or the book is not in the list

get.summary:
Answers with a reading list as a CBL file, to save: the books the caller
is shown, in the list's order, each named by its series, number, volume
and year. Anyone who sees the list can.
get.description:
It is the file `POST /reading-lists/import` reads: an annual's series
ends in "Annual" and a collected edition's in "TPB", which is how the
import tells them from the issue with the same number. A book in no
series is left out, and a book with no number is one entry like the
others of its series that have none.

put.summary:
Makes a page of a book the cover of a reading list, in place of its
first book's cover. Only the owner can. The list's `cover` names the new
image.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The reading list the cover is for

400.description: The page is no picture the server can read

403.description: The caller is not the owner, or the list is not their own

404.description: No such list, no such book, or no such page

delete.summary:
Takes back the cover chosen for a reading list, which shows its first
book's cover again. Nothing happens when none was chosen. Only the owner
can.

204.description: The list shows its first book's cover

403.description: The caller is not the owner, or the list is not their own

put.summary:
Makes a picture the cover of a reading list: the request's body is a
JPEG, PNG, WebP or GIF file of 20 MB at most. Only the owner can.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The reading list the cover is for

400.description: Not a picture the server can read, or one of more than 20 MB

403.description: The caller is not the owner, or the list is not their own

delete.summary:
Takes out of a reading list every book the caller has read to the end.
The others keep their order. Only the one whose list it is can, and the
books go for everyone the list is shared with.
delete.description:
A book the caller is not shown stays: one whose file is gone for now, or
of a library they no longer read.

403.description: The list is someone else's

put.summary:
Says who a reading list is shared with from now on: everyone, the
people named, or nobody. Only the one whose list it is can. The people
it is shared with see it, with the books they may read, and cannot
change it. Someone who may read none of its books does not see it.
put.description:
Everyone named must be on the server: someone who is not refuses the
request, and nothing changes. Naming the one whose list it is changes
nothing.

400.description: Someone named is not on the server

403.description: The list is someone else's

get.summary:
Lists who is reading now, the one who turned a page last first: everyone
whose last page was shown within the last half hour, each with the book
they are in. Only the owner can ask.

403.description: The caller is not the owner

get.summary:
Lists the books the server saw last, newest first. Files that could not
be read are left out.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
How many entries to return at most. 24 when left out, never more
than 100.

get.summary:
Lists the series that hold books in the libraries the caller may read,
the one given a book last first.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
How many entries to return at most. 24 when left out, never more
than 100.

get.summary:
Lists a part of what one scan changed: the books that arrived first,
then the ones that came back, moved and went, each by its paths. Only
the owner can ask.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Lists the changes of one kind only.

schema.description: How a scan found a file changed.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: How many to pass over, from the start of the list.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many to answer with: 100 when left out, 500 at most.

403.description: The caller is not the owner

get.summary:
Searches what the caller may read. Finds the series, books, reading
lists, collections and people that hold every word of `q`, anywhere in a word, and
answers with at most `limit` of each, saying when there are more. A
search with no words finds nothing.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: The words to look for. Case and accents do not matter.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many of each kind to answer with: 50 when left out, and at most.

get.summary: Returns one series.

delete.summary:
Deletes a series that holds no books, with its groups. One that holds
books is refused: move them first. Only the owner can.

403.description: The caller is not the owner

patch.summary:
Gives a series another name. Its books stay in it. A name another series
has is refused: two series are never merged by renaming one. Only the
owner can.

400.description: The name cannot be used

403.description: The caller is not the owner

409.description: Another series of the library has the name; `conflicts_with` is its id

get.summary:
Lists the books of a series in the order they are read: group by group,
as `groups` of the series' overview lists them, with the books in no
group after the limited series and before the annuals. Inside a group
they go by issue number, and the books without one by the date they were
published.

Lists the collections the caller sees that a series is in, in name
order.

put.summary:
Makes a page of a book the cover of a series, in place of its first
book's cover. Only the owner can. The series' `cover` names the new
image.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The series the cover is for

400.description: The page is no picture the server can read

403.description: The caller is not the owner

404.description: No such series, no such book, or no such page

delete.summary:
Takes back the cover chosen for a series, which shows its first book's
cover again. Nothing happens when none was chosen. Only the owner can.

204.description: The series shows its first book's cover

403.description: The caller is not the owner

put.summary:
Makes a picture the cover of a series: the request's body is a JPEG,
PNG, WebP or GIF file of 20 MB at most. Only the owner can.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The series the cover is for

400.description: Not a picture the server can read, or one of more than 20 MB

403.description: The caller is not the owner

post.summary: Adds a group with no books to a series. Only the owner can.

400.description: The number or name is not one a group may have

403.description: The caller is not the owner

409.description: The series has a group of that kind, number and name; `conflicts_with` is its id

get.summary:
Returns one series seen whole, for the page that presents it: what its
books say about it together, how far the caller is through it, and the
book to open next.

Lists the reading lists the caller sees that hold a book of a series, in
name order.

Lists the copies of the database the server keeps in its data
directory, and says whether it makes one every day. Only the owner can
ask.

403.description: The caller is not the owner

post.summary:
Makes a copy of the database now, and removes the oldest when there are
more than are kept. Only the owner can.

403.description: The caller is not the owner

500.description: The copy could not be written

patch.summary:
Turns the daily copy on or off. The copies there are stay. Only the
owner can.

403.description: The caller is not the owner

get.summary:
Says where the server stands with its own updates: the version that
runs, the newer one the last look found, and how far an update that was
asked for is. Only the owner can ask.

403.description: The caller is not the owner

post.summary:
Starts bringing the server to the newer version the last look found,
and answers at once. The version is named, so that the server does not
fetch another one that came out since. The server fetches it, makes sure
Binge signed it, keeps it in its data directory and starts again as it;
requests fail for a moment then. `GET /server/update` says how far it
is, and in `problem` why it stopped when it could not be done. Only the
owner can.

403.description: The caller is not the owner

409.description: An update is under way already, the version is not the newer one the last look found, or this server does not update itself

patch.summary:
Turns the daily look for a newer version on or off. Turning it on looks
at once. A look asks GitHub, where the versions are published, and sends
nothing but the server's version. Only the owner can.

403.description: The caller is not the owner

409.description: The server was started with updates turned off

post.summary:
Looks now whether a newer version is published. The answer says what
was found in `newer`, or in `problem` why the server could not find out:
a look that fails is not an error of this request. Only the owner can.

403.description: The caller is not the owner

409.description: The server was started with updates turned off

post.summary:
First-run setup: makes the owner of a server that has none, and signs
them in. `needs_setup` of `/health` says whether this is still to do.
post.description: What was read before the server had accounts becomes the owner's.

201.description: The owner, signed in: the session cookie is set

400.description: The name or the password will not do

409.description: The server already has an owner

post.summary:
Signs in with a name and password. The answer sets the session cookie,
which is what later requests from the same browser are known by.
post.description:
An app signs in once this way, makes itself a token with `POST /tokens`,
signs out, and uses the token from then on.

200.description: Signed in: the session cookie is set

401.description: The name and password do not match

post.summary:
Ends the session the request came with, and takes its cookie back. A
token is not affected: it is revoked with `DELETE /tokens/{id}`.

get.summary:
Lists the caller's tokens, the newest first. Their secrets are not kept
and so not listed.

post.summary: Makes a token for an app. Its secret is in this answer and nowhere else.

400.description: The name will not do

delete.summary: Revokes one of the caller's tokens. It stops working at once.

get.summary:
Lists, for each series the caller finished a book of and opened none
since, the book that follows, the series read last first. A series the
caller has not read from for some weeks is left out, until it gets a
book, and so is one they took off the list, until they read from it
again.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description:
How many entries to return at most. 24 when left out, never more
than 100.

delete.summary:
Takes a series off the caller's list of `GET /up-next`. It stays off,
also when it gets a book, until the caller reads from it again.

204.description: The series is off the list

get.summary:
Lists everyone who may use the server: the owner, then the others by
name.

post.summary: Adds a user who may read the given libraries.

400.description: The name, the password or a library will not do

get.summary:
Lists everyone on the server by name, the caller too, in name order:
what a person needs to know of the others to share something with
them. It says nothing else about them.

delete.summary:
Removes a user, with their sessions, tokens and reading progress. The
owner cannot be removed.

400.description: The user is the owner

patch.summary:
Gives a user a new password, other libraries to read, or both. Not for
the owner, who reads everything and changes their own password with
`PUT /me/password`.

400.description: The password or a library will not do, or the user is the owner

get.summary:
Lists a part of the series the caller wants to read, the ones put there
last first.
get.description:
A series they have read to the end is left out. It is still theirs to
take off, and it is listed again by itself once it has a book they have
not read.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: How many to pass over, from the start of the list.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many to answer with: 100 when left out, 500 at most.

post.summary:
Puts the series named on the caller's want to read. A series already on
it stays where it was.
post.description:
Every series named must be on the server: one that is not refuses the
request, and nothing is added. One request names 10,000 at most.

400.description: A series named is not on the server

delete.summary: Takes a series off the caller's want to read.

404.description: No such series, or it is not on the caller's want to read

Added.description: What adding books to a list changed.

books.description:
How many books the list gained. The ones it already held are not
counted, and stay where they were.

ApiError.description:
Body of every error response the API sends.

Handlers return it directly. Errors that axum produces on its own (a wrong
method, a body that does not parse) are rewritten into it by
[`json_errors`], so clients only ever have one shape to decode.

conflicts_with.description:
The id of the series, group, reading list or person that is in the
way, when the request clashes with one: the series, the list or the
person that has the name, the group that is the same.

ApiToken.description:
A token an app uses instead of a password. It can do what its user can,
except manage accounts.

created_at.description: When it was made, in seconds since 1970.

last_used_at.description:
When it was last used, in seconds since 1970, to the minute. Missing
when it never was.

name.description: What the person called it, such as the device it is on.

added_at.description: When the server first saw the file, in seconds since 1970.

cover.description:
Name of the book's cover, for `/covers/{cover}`: the one chosen for
it, or else its first page. Missing until the scan has made that.

cover_chosen.description: Whether the cover is one that was chosen for the book.

file_size.description: Size of the file in bytes.

group_id.description:
The group of the series the book is in. Missing for a book that sits
directly in its series.

oneOf.description:
What that group holds. A book of the annuals is called by it:
"Batman Annual #1".

identity.description:
What the book is, computed from its pages. It stays the same when the
file is moved, renamed or retagged. Missing when the file could not be
read. Page images are at `/pages/{identity}/{number}`.

oneOf.description: What the book's file says about itself. Missing when it says nothing.

number.description:
The issue's number where the book sits, such as `12` or `0.5`. It is
the server's own record, not the file's tag, which is `info.number`.

problem.description: Why the file could not be read as a comic.

oneOf.description:
How far the caller has read the book. Missing when they never opened
it past its first page.

published.description:
The date published where the book sits, written `2016`, `2016-07` or
`2016-07-21`: as much as is known. Books with no number are read in
its order.

series_id.description:
The series the book is in. Missing for a file that could not be read:
it is in no series, and `GET /libraries/{id}/unreadable` lists it.

series_name.description:
The name of that series. Away from the series' own page a book is
called by it and its number: "The Flash #12".

BookAfter.description: What comes after a book where it is read.

oneOf.description:
What the book is read as a part of. Missing when it is a part of
nothing: it is in no series and was opened from no list, or it is
not in the list named.

The book to go on to: the first one after it there that can be
read. Missing at the end, and whenever nothing is followed.

BookInfo.description:
What a book's file says about itself, from the `ComicInfo.xml` a tagging
tool put inside it. Each part is missing when the file does not give it.

format.description: The kind of publication, such as `Annual` or `TPB`.

language.description: A language code, such as `en` or `es`.

number.description: The issue's number as written, such as `12`, `0.5` or `Annual 1`.

penciller.description: One name, or several separated by commas.

series.description:
The series the file says it belongs to. The server reads it once, to
place a new book; after that it is only what the file claims, and
`series_id` says where the book is.

writer.description: One name, or several separated by commas.

BooksNamed.description:
Some books, named by what holds them. In a list they go in this order:
the books as named, then the books of the groups, of the series and of
the reading lists, each in the order it is read.

groups.description: Groups to take every book of.

lists.description: Reading lists to take every book of.

series.description: Series to take every book of.

BooksOverview.description:
Some books seen whole, for the caller: the books of a series, or of a
group of one.

first_year.description: The earliest year the books name.

last_year.description: The latest year the books name.

pencillers.description: Who the books name as pencillers, the one most books name first.

publisher.description: The publisher most of the books name.

read.description: How far the caller is through them, and the book to open next.

writers.description:
Who the books name as writers, the one most books name first. Two
spellings of one person are that person, once.

CannotUpdate.description: Why a server does not bring itself to a newer version.

CblEntry.description: One book as a CBL file names it.

number.description: The issue's number, as the file writes it.

volume.description:
The volume, as the file writes it. Most files give the year the
series started.

year.description: The year the issue came out.

CblFound.description: What was found for an entry of a CBL file.

CblHow.description:
How the series of an entry was found. Each way is tried in this order
until one finds the issue.

CblLine.description: One entry of a CBL file, with what the server found for it.

oneOf.description: The book the entry means, when one was found.

candidates.description: The books that fit, when there are several.

oneOf.description: How its series was found. Missing when none was.

rule_id.description:
The rule that decided, when one did: `DELETE
/reading-lists/import/rules/{id}` forgets it.

series_id.description: The series that was looked in.

CblPlan.description: What a reading list made from a CBL file would hold.

lines.description: The file's entries, in its order.

name.description: The name the file gives the list.

name_taken_by.description: The id of the caller's reading list that already has that name.

ChangeKind.description: How a scan found a file changed.

Collection.description:
A collection: series someone picked by hand, from any library, in no
order of their own. It belongs to the person who made it. A series stays
in it under a new name, and leaves it when the series is deleted.

book_count.description: How many books those series hold.

cover.description:
Name of the collection's cover, for `/covers/{cover}`: that of its
first series, by name, that has one.

covers.description:
The covers to show together as one: those of its first series, four
different ones at most.

from_files.description:
Whether the files of a library made it, from a group of series they
name. It is a collection like any other: its owner changes and
deletes it. The files go on putting the series that name the group
in it.

made_by.description: Whose collection it is: the person who made it.

mine.description:
Whether it is the caller's own. Only then can they change it, and
say who it is shared with.

on_home.description:
Whether it is a row on Home, for everyone who sees it. The one whose
collection it is says so. Where the row sits, and whether it is put
away, is each person's own: see `home.rows` in the settings.

series_count.description: How many of its series the caller may read.

shared_with.description:
The people it is shared with one by one, in name order. Only the one
whose collection it is is told: it is empty for anyone else.

shared_with_all.description: Whether everyone on the server sees it.

unread_count.description: How many of those books the caller has not read to the end.

CollectionDetails.description:
What a collection is called and said to be from now on. It is all of
it: without a summary, the collection has none.

name.description:
At most 200 characters. No other collection of the caller's may have
it.

scheduled.description: Whether the server makes a copy every day.

CoverPage.description: A page of a book, to make a cover from.

book_id.description:
The book the page is in. It need not be the book, or a book of the
series, that the cover is for.

CreatedToken.description: A token that was just made, with its secret.

secret.description:
What the app sends as `Authorization: Bearer <secret>`. The server
does not keep it: this answer is the only time it is shown.

name.description: The name to sign in with. Upper and lower case are the same.

Credit.description: Someone books name for a job. `GET /people/{id}` says more about them.

name.description: The name they are shown by, whichever way the books spell it.

DatabaseCopies.description: The copies of the database and how they are made.

folder.description: The folder the copies are in, as a full path on the server.

kept.description: How many copies are kept. Making one more removes the oldest.

scheduled.description: Whether the server makes a copy every day.

DatabaseCopy.description:
One copy of the database: the whole of it as it was at one moment, in a
file that opens like the database itself.

made_at.description: When it was made, in seconds since 1970.

name.description: The file's name in the folder of copies.

ErrorCode.description: What went wrong, as an identifier clients can branch on.

FavoritePage.description:
A favorite page of the caller's, with the book it is a page of.

It belongs to the book's `identity` and the page's number, like
progress: it stays with the page when the book's file is moved or
renamed. Everyone has their own.

added_at.description: When it became a favorite, in seconds since 1970.

page.description:
The page, from 0. Its picture is at `/pages/{identity}/{number}`,
and a small one at `/pages/{identity}/{number}/thumbnail`.

Followed.description: What a book is read as a part of.

FromFiles.description:
What a library makes from what its files say. What it makes is the
owner's, shared with everyone, and from then on a reading list or a
collection like any other. A scan adds what the files it read name, and
takes nothing out. No file is changed.

collections.description:
A collection of each group of series the files name
(`SeriesGroup`).

lists.description:
A reading list of each story arc the files name (`StoryArc` with
`StoryArcNumber`, and `AlternateSeries` with `AlternateNumber`), its
books in the order those numbers give.

Group.description:
A part of a series: one of its volumes, a limited series told under its
name, its annuals, its one-shots, its appearances in other titles, its
collected editions. It may hold no books.

cover.description:
Names the cover image of the book that stands for the group: the
first of its books, in reading order, that has one. Fetch it from
`/covers/{cover}`.

name.description: The group's own name.

number.description:
The number it is known by, when it has one: a volume's, or for
annuals that of the volume they are of.

unread_count.description: How many of its books the caller has not read to the end.

GroupKind.description: What a group of a series holds.

GroupName.description:
What a group is known by from now on. It is all of it: what is left out,
the group does not have.

name.description:
A name of its own, of at most 200 characters: a limited series'
title, or the other title a group of appearances is in. Any kind may
have one.

number.description:
A number to know it by, from 1 to 65535: a volume's, or for annuals
that of the volume they are of. Any kind may have one.

series.description: The series it is a part of.

GroupOverview.description:
A group of a series seen whole, for the page that presents it: what its
books say about it together, and how far the caller is through it. What
to open next follows what they did last in this group, whatever they
read elsewhere.

built_at.description:
When the server was built, in seconds since 1970. With `commit`, it
tells one build from another of the same version.

commit.description:
The commit the server was built from, with a `+` after it when files
differed from that commit. Missing, like `built_at`, in a build made
without the build scripts.

name.description: Product name of the server.

needs_setup.description:
Whether the server still waits for its owner to be made with
`POST /setup`. Until then nobody can sign in.

HeldFile.description: A file of a book the library holds more than once.

path.description: Where the file is, from the library's folder.

HeldTwice.description: A book the library holds more than once.

files.description: Its files, in the order of their paths: two at least.

Letter.description: A letter that the names of series start with.

count.description: How many series start with it.

letter.description:
A capital from A to Z, or `#` for every name that starts with
anything else. A name is filed without its accent: `Élodie` under E.

offset.description:
Where the first of them is in the list by name: the `offset` to ask
`GET /libraries/{id}/series` for it with.

Library.description: A folder of comics the server was pointed at.

oneOf.description: What it makes from what its files say. Only the owner is told.

last_scanned_at.description: When the last scan finished, in seconds since 1970.

path.description: The folder, as a full path on the server. Only the owner is told.

set_aside_count.description:
How many of the files that could not be read the owner set aside.
Only the owner is told.

unreadable_count.description:
How many of its files could not be read and are still to look at.
`GET /libraries/{id}/unreadable` lists them. Only the owner is told.

LibraryChoices.description:
What the series of a library can be narrowed by: every value its books
have.

pencillers.description: The one most series name first.

publishers.description: The one most series have first.

writers.description: The one most series name first.

position.description:
Where the book goes among the list's books as `GET
/reading-lists/{id}/books` gives them, from 0. Past the end is the
end.

books.description:
How many books the mark changed. The ones that already were as asked
are not counted.

NamedDecade.description: Ten years the series of a library can be narrowed by.

first_year.description: The first of the ten years, such as `1990`. Ask for them as `1990s`.

series_count.description: How many series of the library have a book from them.

NamedPerson.description: Someone the series of a library can be narrowed by.

series_count.description: How many series of the library have a book that names them.

NamedPublisher.description: A publisher the series of a library can be narrowed by.

series_count.description: How many series of the library have a book of theirs.

NewCblRule.description: What the caller says an entry of a CBL file means.

book_id.description: The book that this one entry is.

entry.description:
The entry, as the file writes it. A rule about a series goes by the
entry's series and volume, and holds for every number.

series_id.description:
The series that the entry's series is: its issues are looked for
there. Give this or `book_id`, not both.

name.description:
At most 200 characters. No other collection of the caller's may have
it: names that differ only in capitals, accents, spaces or
punctuation count as the same.

series.description: The series the collection starts with.

name.description:
A name of its own, of at most 200 characters: a limited series'
title, or the other title a group of appearances is in. Any kind may
have one.

number.description:
A number to know it by, from 1 to 65535: a volume's, or for annuals
that of the volume they are of. Any kind may have one.

oneOf.description:
What it makes from what its files say. Left out, it makes nothing
until it is asked to.

name.description: Name to show. Defaults to the folder's name.

path.description:
Full path of the folder on the server. A leading `~` means the home
folder of the account the server runs as.

name.description: One more way of writing the person's name.

books.description:
The books the list starts with, in this order: these books as named,
then the books of the groups, of the series and of the reading lists
named, each in the order it is read.

groups.description: Groups to take every book of.

lists.description: Reading lists to take every book of.

name.description:
At most 200 characters. No other list of the caller's may have it:
names that differ only in capitals, accents, spaces or punctuation
count as the same.

series.description: Series to take every book of.

name.description: What to call it, such as the device it is for.

libraries.description: Ids of the libraries the user may read. None when left out.

name.description: The name to sign in with. Upper and lower case are the same.

password.description:
At least 8 characters. The owner tells it to the person, who can
change it once signed in.

NewerVersion.description: A version newer than the one that runs.

notes.description: The page that says what changed in it.

NotUpdating.description:
Why a server does not bring itself to a newer version, for a program
and for a person.

message.description: The same in a sentence for the owner.

OnHome.description: Whether a collection is a row on Home from now on.

byte_size.description:
Size of the image in bytes. For a page of a PDF that the server
draws, the size of what the page is made from, not of the picture
sent.

height.description: Height in pixels. Missing when `width` is.

width.description:
Width in pixels. Missing until a scan has read it, and for an image
the server cannot understand.

PagedBooks.description: A part of a list of books.

total.description: How many books the whole list holds.

PagedFavoritePages.description: A part of the caller's favorite pages.

total.description: How many pages the whole list holds.

PagedPeople.description: A part of a list of people.

total.description: How many people the whole list holds.

PagedSeries.description: A part of a list of series.

total.description: How many series the whole list holds.

current.description: The password as it is now.

new.description: The password to have from now on. At least 8 characters.

people.description: The ids of the people to make one with this one: 50 at most.

Person.description:
A person the books name as a writer or a penciller, counted over the
books the caller may read. Someone none of those books names is not
there for the caller.

Files spell one person several ways, so a person is the names they go
by. Two spellings that differ only in capitals, accents, spaces or
punctuation are one name from the start; the owner makes the rest one.

book_count.description: Books that name them, for whatever job.

name.description: The name they are shown by: one of their names.

pencilled_count.description: Books that name them as a penciller.

written_count.description: Books that name them as a writer.

shown_by.description: The id of the one of their names to show them by.

names.description: Their names, the one they are shown by first.

PersonDetails.description: A person with every name they go by.

PersonName.description: One way of writing a person's name.

Place.description:
Where a book is to sit. It is the whole place: what is left out, the book
does not have.

group_id.description:
A group of that series. Without one the book sits directly in its
series.

number.description: The issue's number, such as `12` or `0.5`. At most 32 characters.

series_id.description: A series of the library the book's file is in.

Progress.description:
How far the caller has read a book. Everyone has their own.

It belongs to the book's `identity`, so it stays with the book when its
file is moved or renamed, and two files with the same pages share it.

completed.description: Whether that was the book's last page.

updated_at.description: When this was saved, in seconds since 1970.

ReadMark.description: Which books to mark, and how.

groups.description: Groups to mark every book of.

lists.description: Reading lists to mark every book of.

read.description: `true` marks the books as read to the end, `false` as never opened.

series.description: Series to mark every book of.

ReadSoFar.description: How far the caller is through some books: a series, or a group of one.

books_read.description: Books the caller read to the end, out of `readable_count`.

oneOf.description:
The book to open to go on with them. It follows what the caller did
last among these books: a book they left unfinished, or after one
they finished, the first unfinished book behind it, or at the end the
first unfinished one anywhere. Someone who read nothing, or
everything, starts at the first book in reading order: when
`books_read` is `readable_count`, this is where to read them again.
Missing when none of the books can be read.

pages_read.description: Pages the caller has been through, over all the books.

readable_count.description:
How many of the books can be read. The rest are files the server
could not understand.

seconds_left.description:
How long the pages not yet read will take the caller, in seconds, at
their own pace: the time a page took them over their latest
sittings. Missing until they have read enough here to tell.

pages.description: Pages of those books gone through.

day.description: The day on the caller's clock, as `2026-11-18`.

ReadingList.description:
A reading list: books in an order someone chose, across series. It
belongs to the person who made it, and holds its books by their
`identity`: a book stays in it when its file is moved or renamed, and
comes back into it when a file that was gone is seen again.

book_count.description: How many of its books are on the server now and the caller may read.

cover.description:
Name of the list's cover, for `/covers/{cover}`: the one chosen for
it, or else the cover of its first book that has one.

cover_chosen.description: Whether the cover is one that was chosen for the list.

covers.description:
The covers to show together as one: those of its first books, four
different ones at most. None when a cover was chosen for the list.

first_year.description: The earliest year its books came out.

from_files.description:
Whether the files of a library made it, from a story arc they name.
It is a list like any other: its owner changes and deletes it. The
files go on putting the books that name the arc in it.

last_year.description: The latest year its books came out.

made_by.description: Whose list it is: the person who made it.

mine.description:
Whether it is the caller's own. Only then can they change it, and
say who it is shared with.

shared_with.description:
The people it is shared with one by one, in name order. Only the one
whose list it is is told: it is empty for anyone else.

shared_with_all.description: Whether everyone on the server sees it.

unread_count.description: How many of those the caller has not read to the end.

ReadingListDetails.description:
What a list is called and said to be from now on. It is all of it:
without a summary, the list has none.

name.description: At most 200 characters. No other list of the caller's may have it.

ReadingListOverview.description:
A reading list seen whole, for the page that presents it: what its books
say together, and how far the caller is through it. What to open next
follows what they did last among its books, whatever they read
elsewhere.

ReadingMonth.description: A month the caller read in.

page.description: The page they were shown last, from 0.

user_name.description: What the person signs in with.

ReadingYear.description:
What the caller read in one year. It is told from their reading itself,
a stretch of pages at a time: marking a book read adds nothing to it.

books.description: Books read from over the whole year.

days.description: The days they read, in order. A day without reading is left out.

first_year.description: The first year the caller read in. Missing when they never read.

months.description: The months they read in, in order.

writers.description: The ten writers they read most, the one with most books first.

Removed.description: What taking the read books out of a list changed.

books.description: How many books the list lost.

page.description: The last page shown, from 0. With two pages on screen, the later one.

ScanChange.description: One file a scan found changed.

oneOf.description:
The book as the library holds it now. Missing when it holds it no
longer, and for a file that could not be read.

from_path.description: Where a moved file was before.

path.description:
Where the file is, from the library's folder, or where it was for
one that is gone.

ScanChanges.description: A part of what one scan changed.

total.description: How many changes the whole list holds.

ScanRecord.description:
A scan that changed what a library holds, with how many files of each
kind it found changed.

back.description: Books the library held before, gone since, and here again.

ended_at.description: When it had gone through the folder.

gone.description: Books whose file is no longer there.

moved.description: Books whose file is at another path.

started_at.description: When it started, in seconds since 1970.

ScanStatus.description:
Where a library's scan stands. After a scan ends, its numbers stay until
the next one starts.

found.description: Comic files seen in the folder so far.

problem.description: What went wrong in the last scan.

to_analyze.description: Books that need their covers made in this scan.

books.description:
Books found by their name, title, series, writer, penciller or
publisher, in name order.

collections.description: Collections found by their name, in name order.

lists.description: Reading lists found by their name, in name order.

more_books.description: Whether more books were found than are listed.

more_collections.description: Whether more collections were found than are listed.

more_lists.description: Whether more reading lists were found than are listed.

more_people.description: Whether more people were found than are listed.

more_series.description: Whether more series were found than are listed.

people.description: People found by any name they go by, the ones most books name first.

series.description: Series found by their name, in name order.

Series.description:
A series of a library: the books that go by one name. The server keeps
it as its own record. It is not a folder, and a book stays in its series
when its file is moved, renamed or retagged. It may hold no books: a
series stays until it is deleted.

cover.description:
Name of the series' cover, for `/covers/{cover}`: the one chosen for
it, or else the cover of its first book in reading order. Missing
until a book has one.

cover_chosen.description: Whether the cover is one that was chosen for the series.

unread_count.description: How many of its books the caller has not read to the end.

wanted.description:
Whether the caller put it on their want to read. It stays so until
they take it off, also once they have read all of it.

SeriesAdded.description: What adding series to a collection, or to want to read, changed.

series.description: How many series it gained. The ones it already held are not counted.

name.description:
At most 200 characters. No other series of the library may have it:
names that differ only in capitals, accents, spaces or punctuation
count as the same.

groups.description:
Its groups, in the order they are read, the ones that hold no books
included. Empty when it has none.

SeriesOverview.description:
A series seen whole, for the page that presents it: what its books say
about it together, and how far the caller is through it.

settings.description:
Each value under its key. The server keeps a value and does not read
it: the app that wrote it knows what it means.

Sharing.description:
Who a reading list or a collection is shared with from now on. It is
all of it: the people left out no longer see it.

everyone.description: Whether everyone on the server sees it, those who join later too.

people.description:
Ids of the people it is shared with one by one, from `GET
/users/names`.

Summary.description:
What some books are about. No file describes a series or a group, so
these are the words of the first of the books, in reading order, that
describes itself.

oneOf.description:
The book the words are from. Missing for a reading list, whose
summary is its own.

looks.description: Whether the server looks for a newer version by itself, once a day.

UpdateStage.description: Where an update asked for stands.

UpdateStatus.description: Where the server stands with its own updates.

oneOf.description:
Why this server does not bring itself to a newer version. Missing
when it does.

looked_at.description:
When the server last looked, in seconds since 1970. Missing when it
has not looked since it started.

looks.description:
Whether the server looks for a newer version by itself, once a day.
Looking asks GitHub, so it is off until the owner turns it on.

oneOf.description: The newer version the last look found.

not_started.description:
A newer version that is kept in the data directory and was not
started when this server was, in a sentence for the owner. Missing
when there is none. It stays until the server starts again.

problem.description:
What went wrong the last time the server looked or tried to update,
in a sentence for the owner.

version.description:
The version to bring the server to: the newer one the last look
found, as `newer.version` says it.

User.description: A person who may use the server.

created_at.description: When the account was made, in seconds since 1970.

libraries.description:
Ids of the libraries the person may read: every library for the
owner, the ones the owner gave them for a member.

name.description: What the person signs in with.

UserChange.description: What to change about a user. What is left out stays as it is.

libraries.description: Ids of the libraries the user may read from now on.

password.description: A new password. It ends the user's sessions; their tokens stay.

UserName.description: A person of the server as the others know them: by name.

session.name: binge_session
session.description: The cookie that signing in sets. What the web UI uses.

token.description: An API token, made with `POST /tokens`. What apps use.
